add.title: Problems of Industrial Development in India – Mains Checklist
add.md:
# Why Indian industry has under-performed
- **Stagnant manufacturing share:** manufacturing stuck around **15-17% of GVA** for three decades; National Manufacturing Policy 2011 target of **25% of GDP by 2022** was missed.
  - **Premature deindustrialisation** (Dani Rodrik): services overtook industry before manufacturing peaked.
- **Infrastructure deficit:** power, transport and port bottlenecks cause **capacity under-utilisation** (RBI OBICUS survey usually shows about **74-76%**).
  - **Logistics cost** about **7.8-8.9% of GDP** (NCAER-DPIIT estimate, 2023) – answer: National Logistics Policy (Sept 2022), PM Gati Shakti (Oct 2021).
- **Factor-market rigidities:** costly, slow **land acquisition** (RFCTLARR Act 2013); rigid labour laws, now replaced by **four Labour Codes** (in force **21 Nov 2025**).
- **Finance:** high cost of capital; **MSME credit gap**; twin balance-sheet problem (2014-18) hit investment.
- **Technology and scale:** low **R&D spend (about 0.65% of GDP)**; too many tiny firms ("**missing middle**") – about 96% of non-farm units are proprietorships.
- **Import dependence:** electronics components, solar cells, and about **70% of APIs** (bulk drugs) from **China** – PLI schemes and Press Note 3 (2020) respond.
- **Regional imbalance:** industry concentrated in **Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka**; backward regions lag.
- **Public sector issues:** loss-making CPSEs, political pricing → disinvestment and **New PSE Policy 2021**.
- **Jobless growth:** capital-intensive growth; contract workers about **42%** of factory workers (ASI).
- **Industrial sickness** and delayed payments to MSMEs (MSME Samadhaan, TReDS).
# Andhra Pradesh angle
- Loss of the **Hyderabad** industrial and services base at bifurcation (2014); manufacturing only about **11% of GSDP**.
- Responses: **IDP (4.0) 2024-29** (Rs 30 lakh crore target), Single Desk Portal (21-day clearances), VCIC/CBIC/HBIC nodes, 175+ MSME parks.
> Mains answer frame: problem → evidence (number) → policy response (Make in India 2014, PLI 2020, NLP 2022, Labour Codes 2025). Trap: capacity under-use is mainly due to infrastructure, not lack of demand alone.
~~ Sources: DPIIT/NCAER logistics cost report 2023; PIB (Labour Codes in force 21 Nov 2025; National Logistics Policy 2022); RBI OBICUS releases; Economic Survey 2025-26; app notes 3:104

add.title: Forest Strategies, Schemes and Programmes in Andhra Pradesh
add.md:
# Goals and administration
- **Department:** Environment, Forests, Science & Technology – minister **Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan** (since 2024).
- **Green-cover goal (Swarna Andhra @2047):** about **30%** green cover in 2025 (recorded forest ~23% + trees outside forests ~7%) → **37% by 2029-30** → **50% by 2047**.
  - Needs over **32,000 sq km** of extra green cover; a State **Greening Society** was proposed (2025) to drive it.
# Plantation programmes
- **Vanam-Manam:** State plantation drive relaunched on **World Environment Day, 5 June 2025**; target about **5.58 crore saplings** on **1.8 lakh ha** in 2025; tied to **Vana Mahotsavam**.
- **Seed-ball drive:** about **2.06 crore seed balls** over **20,929 ha** of degraded forest (2025).
- **Trees Outside Forests (TOFI):** MoEFCC + USAID programme; AP one of **7** States (Nov 2022).
- **Nagar Van Yojana** (Centre, **2020**): urban forests in municipal areas; AP towns develop **Nagara Vanams** (e.g. near Tirupati, Visakhapatnam).
# Community forest management
- **Vana Samrakshana Samithis (VSS):** village forest-protection committees under **Joint Forest Management**, which AP took up in the early **1990s** with World Bank support (AP Forestry Project), later **Community Forest Management (CFM)**.
  - VSS members protect forests and share **NTFP** and part of timber income; tribal produce bought by **GCC**.
- **Forest Rights Act 2006:** individual and community titles to tribals in the agency areas.
# Funds and centrally sponsored schemes
- **CAMPA** (Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act 2016): State CAMPA funds afforestation for forest land diverted to projects.
- **Green India Mission** (2014; one of the 8 NAPCC missions), **MISHTI** (mangroves, 5 June 2023 – Coringa, Krishna estuary), **Nagar Van Yojana**.
# Protection and conflict
- **Red Sanders Anti-Smuggling Task Force (RSASTF)**, Tirupati (2015): guards endemic red sanders in Seshachalam.
- **Human-elephant conflict** (Chittoor, Parvathipuram Manyam): **Karnataka** handed **kumki elephants** to AP (2025) under an inter-State MoU.
- **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve** = India's **largest tiger reserve** by area; eco-tourism (Nallamala, Papikonda, Maredumilli) earns local income.
> Exam angle: green-cover targets (37% → 50% by 2047), Vanam-Manam, VSS = JFM, RSASTF = red sanders. Trap: plantation drives add tree cover, not natural forest cover.
~~ Sources: Business Standard / The Week (5 Jun 2025, AP plantation drive, 50% by 2047); Deccan Chronicle (seed-ball drive; Greening Society); forests.ap.gov.in; Lok Sabha reply on Nagar Van Yojana; AP SES 2024-25

add.title: AP IT & GCC Policy (4.0) 2024-29 – Models and Incentives
add.md:
# The policy
- **AP Information Technology & Global Capability Centres (GCC) Policy (4.0) 2024-29:** approved by Cabinet early Dec 2024; issued **12 December 2024** by the **ITE&C Department**; operational guidelines **G.O.Ms.No.10, 1 May 2025**.
- **Aim:** make AP a **global knowledge-economy and talent hub**; "**saturation-level jobs in all districts**"; deep tech (AI, cyber security, automation); remote, gig and hybrid work; links to **"One Family, One Entrepreneur"** (Swarna Andhra @2047).
- Wider goal: Minister **Nara Lokesh** targets about **5 lakh** IT and electronics jobs within the **20 lakh jobs** promise.
- **GCC** = a multinational's **own offshore unit** serving its parent (not an outsourcing vendor).
# Three infrastructure models
- **Model 1 – Co-working spaces** (Tier I/II cities): facility of at least **100 seats / 10,000 sq ft**; capital subsidy **50% of capex, up to Rs 2,000 per sq ft**; lease support Rs 2,000 per seat for 6 months.
- **Model 2 – Neighbourhood workspaces** (Tier I, II, III towns): small units of **10 seats / 1,000 sq ft** in government buildings, apartments, schools – "work near home"; subsidy 50%, up to **Rs 1,000 per sq ft**.
- **Model 3 – IT campus developers:** at least **5 lakh sq ft**; 50% subsidy up to Rs 2,000 per sq ft, industrial power tariff, road access, mixed use up to 33%.
- First co-working hubs: **Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Tirupati**.
# Incentives for IT firms and GCCs
- **Eligibility:** IT turnover at least **Rs 30 crore** or **50+ employees**, kept for **18 months**.
- **Job-creation subsidy:** **Rs 1.5 lakh** per AP graduate; **Rs 3 lakh** for NIRF top-10 graduates or experienced hires; **100% employer EPF share (6 months)** for women, BC, SC, ST and transgender staff.
- **Rental subsidy** Rs 2,000 per seat for 24 months; power at industrial tariff with **Re 1/unit discount for 5 years**; HRA/education allowance up to **Rs 1 lakh per employee for 3 years**.
- **Tailor-made** incentives for **2,000+ jobs or 1 million sq ft**; **Early Bird:** rent-free government buildings for **5 years**.
- **Future Skills Credit Scheme** for upskilling; approvals via **SIPB** (CM) and SIPC.
# Companion policies (4.0 suite)
- **LIFT Policy 4.0** (Land Incentive for Tech Hubs) – land for GCCs and IT parks; e.g. **TCS** given land in Visakhapatnam at a token **99 paise** lease (2025).
- **Data Centre Policy 4.0** (Nov 2024) – Google's **1 GW** AI hub, Visakhapatnam; **Innovation and Startup Policy 4.0** – 20,000 startups; **Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0** – US$50 bn output.
- **Earlier:** IT Policy 2014-20 (after bifurcation), **IT Policy 2021-24** (local procurement up to Rs 1 crore from AP firms; entry-level job = CTC up to Rs 5 lakh).
> Exam angle: 12 Dec 2024, three models (co-working, neighbourhood, campus), GCC meaning, LIFT full form. Trap: the startup policy belongs to ITE&C, not Industries & Commerce.
~~ Sources: Rödl & Partner "Andhra Pradesh IT & GCC Policy (2024-2029)" (Mar 2025); Khaitan & Co / Mondaq summaries; newsonair.gov.in (Cabinet approval); apchambers.in (G.O.Ms.10 guidelines); Republic World (99-paise TCS lease, 5 lakh jobs aim)
